finding.title: Reviewer no_go from the pre-repair tree is final; the fix loop can never recover the verdict
finding.evidence: runner.py:5444 captures the reviewer verdict from the review STAGE, which runs on the pre-merge worktree before the delivery-time deterministic repairs (5528), proof (5610) and `_fix_loop` (5632). After repair, runner.py:5683-5700 AND-combines: `if verdict == 'go' and re_verdict == 'go'` else `verdict = 'no_go'` — a reviewer no_go can never be upgraded by the post-repair rescore. But the reviewer's verdict is NOT primarily brief-aware: agents/reviewer.py:149-166 computes `verdict = score >= GO_THRESHOLD` where score is the same structural `heuristic_score` used by `_rescore_delivered` (runner.py:2670-2676), at most blended 70/30 with an optional LLM score. So a pre-repair structural gap (missing entrypoint + unparseable package.json = 55 < 60) that `_fill_missing`/`_deterministic_repairs`/the improver then fix keeps the build no_go even after proof passes and the identical heuristic re-scores 'go'. Additionally `_rescore_delivered`'s catch-all (runner.py:2678-2680) returns ('no_go', 0.0, []) on any exception, flipping a reviewer 'go' to no_go via the same AND.
finding.win_rate_impact: Every build where codegen leaves a structurally-deficient tree that the post-merge fix loop successfully repairs (the exact ~14%-go-rate class the loop was built for, per its own docstring at runner.py:4115) still finishes no_go: up to 6 improver attempts / 720s of budget are spent reaching a green proof and then discarded by a stale verdict. Correct, repaired work is graded as failure — a direct, recurring win-rate loss on the default path.
finding.fix: When the tree changed after the review stage (fix_attempt_* recorded, or delivered tree signature differs from the reviewed source_tree_sha256 captured at runner.py:5447-5456), re-run the reviewer (or recompute heuristic_score + the LLM blend) against the delivered tree and use THAT verdict in the AND-combine, instead of honoring the stale one. Also make `_rescore_delivered`'s exception path return a 'skipped' sentinel that keeps the reviewer verdict rather than fail-closed no_go.

finding.title: Best-of-N candidates are proofed without build/tests, so a winner that doesn't compile can be picked
finding.evidence: best_of_n.py:320-326 calls `proof_run(cand.worktree.dir, checklist=..., execution_backend=..., stack=...)` with no `run_tests`/`run_build`/`brief`, and proof_run defaults are `run_tests=False, run_build=False` (proof_run.py:3898-3900). Every other proof in the pipeline (stage_debug.py:48-57, runner.py:5610-5620, fix loop 4274-4283) passes `run_generated_build=True`/`run_generated_tests=True` from settings. With structural-only proofs, both candidates typically land in the `proof_passed` class and `rank_key` (best_of_n.py:88-97) picks by source_bytes — a fatter tree that fails `npm run build` beats a leaner one that compiles. `best_of_n` defaults to 2 (settings.py:440), so this is the default code path.
finding.win_rate_impact: The build pays for N full codegen trajectories to buy selection quality, then selects nearly blind: the merged 'winner' first hits a real build at stage-debug/delivery proof, fails, and burns the debug attempts plus the fix-loop budget (and can end no_go) while a discarded candidate would have passed outright. Directly converts would-be wins into repair-loop losses and wasted spend on every default build where trajectories diverge in buildability.
finding.fix: Thread the same proof knobs into sampling: pass `run_build=settings.run_generated_build`, `build_timeout`, `run_tests=settings.run_generated_tests`, `test_timeout`, and `brief` through `bon.sample` into its `proof_run` call (runner.py:6349-6360 already has settings in scope), so candidate ranking uses the same objective proof the delivered tree must later pass.

finding.title: Visual liveness gate bypasses posture: any console error or vision 'no' = unconditional no_go

The posture system is silently bypassed.

finding.title: Sandbox _exec timeout kill leaks the Windows process tree and can hang the whole build
finding.evidence: settings.py:699 defaults execution_backend='auto', so `_new_sandbox_runner` (proof_run.py:1169-1177) always builds a SandboxRunner and `_run_proof_command` takes the sandbox path — the carefully fixed local fallback with `_kill_tree` (taskkill /PID /T /F, proof_run.py:1268-1293) is dead code in the default config. sandbox.py:308-317 `_exec` on timeout calls only `proc.kill()` (kills npm.cmd's cmd.exe, not the node grandchildren that inherit the pipes) then `await proc.communicate()` with NO timeout — it blocks until every grandchild closes stdout/stderr. proof_run.py:1249-1251 (`asyncio.run(_run_sandbox())`, no outer bound) then never returns.
finding.win_rate_impact: Any timed-out npm install/build/test on Windows (registry stall, a build script that opens a watcher) hangs the entire proof — the build burns its whole wall-clock budget and dies as a timeout instead of completing with a recorded degraded step. Orphaned node processes also keep node_modules locked, making the NEXT build's npm install fail EPERM/EBUSY — cascading false build failures.
finding.fix: Port proof_run's `_kill_tree` into sandbox `_exec`: on timeout run `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` on Windows (killpg on POSIX), then bound the drain (`asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), 10)` with a fallback to empty output).

(1) Routing: D:\skyn3t2.0\skyn3t\config\settings.py:699 `execution_backend: Literal["auto","docker","inline"] = "auto"`; D:\skyn3t2.0\skyn3t\studio\proof_run.py:3896 `proof_run(..., execution_backend: str = "auto")`; `_new_sandbox_runner` (proof_run.py:1169-1178) returns None only for "inline", so the default always builds a SandboxRunner and `_run_proof_command` (1216) takes the sandbox branch — the local fallback with `_kill_tree` (1268-1326) is dead code in the default config (reachable only via inline backend or SandboxRunner import failure). (2) Mechanism: D:\skyn3t2.0\skyn3t\security\sandbox.py:305-317 — on `asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout)` TimeoutError (reachable: requires-python >=3.11 where asyncio.TimeoutError is builtin TimeoutError), `_exec` calls only `proc.kill()` then `await proc.communicate()` with NO bound. On Windows `resolve_executable` (skyn3t/exec_paths.py:63-95) maps npm→npm.cmd, which CreateProcess runs under cmd.exe; node grandchildren inherit the stdout/stderr pipe write handles, TerminateProcess kills only cmd.exe, and communicate() waits for pipe EOF, i.e. until every grandchild exits — indefinitely for a stalled install or watcher. No taskkill/killpg exists anywhere in sandbox.py (grep confirmed). (3) Hang propagation, both branches: proof runs in a thread via `asyncio.to_thread(proof_run, ...)` (skyn3t/studio/improve.py:146), so no running loop → proof_run.py:1248-1249 `asyncio.run(_run_sandbox())` with no outer bound, exactly as cited. And `_proof_run_without_blocking` (improve.py:148-161) deliberately awaits the worker even on cancellation, so the build cannot even be cancelled cleanly. (4) Not already handled: the docker-backend container cleanup (sandbox.py:222-232) runs only AFTER `_exec` returns and only for backend=docker (where killing the docker CLI closes the pipes, so that path drains fine); the subprocess fallback — the exact auto-without-Docker path — has no equivalent. (5) No test pins the `_exec` timeout branch: test_sandbox_docker_timeout_removes_named_container (tests/test_iter5_fixes.py:56-83) fakes `_exec` entirely; tests/test_platform.py:135-174 and test_iter5_fixes.py:86-117 run real `_exec` only on the happy path. One correction to the proposed fix: bare `os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), SIGKILL)` on POSIX would be wrong as stated — `_exec`'s create_subprocess_exec does not pass start_new_session, so the child shares skyn3t's own process group and killpg would kill the whole application; the spawn must gain start_new_session first (proof_run's fallback does exactly this at 1296-1298 before its killpg).
verdict.refined_fix: Minimal change, confined to `_exec` in D:\skyn3t2.0\skyn3t\security\sandbox.py (fixes docker, subprocess, and any future backend in one place). (a) Spawn with its own process group on POSIX so tree-kill is safe: add `start_new_session=(os.name != "nt")` to the `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(...)` call at lines 293-299 (the kwarg is accepted-and-ignored on Windows, but the guard documents intent). (b) In the timeout branch (lines 308-317), BEFORE the existing `proc.kill()` (taskkill /T must enumerate the tree while the root is alive — same order as proof_run._kill_tree): on Windows `await asyncio.to_thread(subprocess.run, ["taskkill", "/PID", str(proc.pid), "/T", "/F"], check=False, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=10)` wrapped in try/except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError); on POSIX `os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGKILL)` wrapped in try/except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError, OSError). Keep `proc.kill()` as the backstop. (c) Bound the drain: replace `out, err = await proc.communicate()` with `out, err = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=10)`; keep the existing `except Exception: out, err = b"", b"timeout"` (which now also catches the wait_for TimeoutError). No other lines change — the exit-code line 321 already maps returncode None to -1, and `_run_docker`'s timed_out container cleanup contract is unchanged. finding.title: Applied tuning evaporates on restart while its APPLIED record dedupe-blocks re-application forever
finding.evidence: handlers.py:103-139 _apply_tuning writes only to the in-memory overrides dict and live Settings via setattr — it never calls tuning_store.persist_overrides (tuning_store.py:43-45 even documents 'the serve/cortex process persists on approval', but no serve-path caller exists; grep shows persist_overrides only in cli/main.py and the opt-in ratchet evaluator, bootstrap.py:101). Meanwhile the proposal is mirrored to proposals.jsonl and reloaded on boot (bootstrap.py:169-172), and proposal_store.py:140-149 treats APPLIED as a blocking dedupe status forever.
finding.win_rate_impact: With default settings (ratchet off, cortex_auto_approve_safe on), GatedTuner's best_of_n bump or a human-approved 'enable learned router' (RoutingReadiness auto_route/model_evolution) takes effect in-process only. The system permanently believes an improvement is enacted that no build actually gets — the tuning loop is dead after the first restart, and quality-raising knobs (best_of_n, learned routing) stay at defaults forever.
finding.fix: In _apply_tuning, after computing 'observed', call persist_overrides(self.data_dir, {k: v for k, v in observed.items() if k in PERSISTABLE_TUNING}); for keys that cannot be persisted (autonomy flags), return the result with a durable=False marker and make ProposalStore._is_duplicate not treat such APPLIED records as blocking.

finding.title: Constant dedupe key makes GatedTuner's progressive best_of_n escalation one-shot
finding.evidence: components.py:106-116 — GatedTuner submits the tuning proposal with a fixed title ('increase best_of_n after repeated low stage scores') and no dedupe_key, so Proposal.__post_init__ derives the same key every time (proposal_store.py:84). Once one bump is APPLIED, _is_duplicate (proposal_store.py:140-149) blocks the next bump (value 3, 4, ...) as a duplicate — even within the same process, and across restarts via the persisted JSONL store.
finding.win_rate_impact: The designed escalation ladder (bump best_of_n one notch each time a stage keeps scoring under 70, up to 8) can only ever fire once per installation. Stages that keep failing after the first bump get no further trajectory sampling, so the intended low-score -> more-samples -> higher-go-rate mechanism silently stops at +1; combined with the non-persistence defect it stops at +0 after a restart.
finding.fix: Give the proposal a value-bearing dedupe key, e.g. dedupe_key=f"tuning:best_of_n:{min(current + 1, 8)}", so each distinct target value is a distinct proposal while identical open/applied values still dedupe.

verdict.evidence: components.py:106-116 submits the TUNING proposal with a fixed title and no dedupe_key; Proposal.__post_init__ (proposal_store.py:83-84) derives the constant key "tuning:increase best_of_n after repeated low stage scores" regardless of payload value. In D:\skyn3t2.0\skyn3t\cortex\components.py, GatedTuner._consider, compute the target once and give the proposal a value-bearing dedupe key. Replace lines 106-116 with:

finding.title: Default ratchet evaluator benches with no budget guard, no budget reset, unlike production builds
finding.evidence: bootstrap.py:111-126 — the auto-ratchet build_fn constructs StudioRunner(event_bus, orchestrator, settings=..., memory=..., rag=..., skills=...) with no cost_tracker, no budget_guard, no learning/patterns, and never resets the LLM budget between cases. The CLI's equivalent (_make_ratchet_build_fn, cli/main.py:794-818) deliberately wires _build_observability(...) and calls _reset_bench_budget per case. The evaluator runs all_cases(data_dir) — 20 default cases plus up to 200 captured regressions (studio/bench.py:474-483) — TWICE per auto-approved tuning proposal (ratchet.py:109-113), all spending against the shared adapter budget that raises BudgetExceeded past daily_usd_cap (adapters/llm.py:1324-1330).
finding.win_rate_impact: Two concrete paths: (1) the before-run consumes the daily cap, so after-run cases increasingly die on BudgetExceeded -> after go_rate is artificially lower -> gate_change reverts genuinely good tuning (or, when both runs are equally budget-poisoned, keeps a change on garbage evidence); (2) one auto-approved GatedTuner proposal can trigger 40-440 unguarded real builds that exhaust the daily budget, after which real user builds fail on the cap for the rest of the day.
finding.fix: Mirror the CLI in _make_default_ratchet_evaluator: build cost_tracker/budget_guard via _build_observability-equivalents, reset the per-build budget before each bench case, pass learning/patterns so the bench matches the production pipeline, and cap the ratchet case list (e.g. built_in_cases('apps') plus a bounded regression sample).

finding.title: Tournament solo plays are automatic wins, making learned-router confidence vacuous
finding.evidence: record_win with losers=[] counts wins+=1, plays+=1 with no Elo exchange (model_tournament.py:196-200), and _feed_tournament records a solo win for every stage that merely returned success — inside `if result.success:` at runner.py:5351/5366 — regardless of the build's final verdict. So every model fed by real traffic has win_rate exactly 1.0 and rating pinned at 1000. RoutingRecommender's gate (min_plays=5, min_win_rate=0.55, routing_recommendations.py:63) is therefore satisfied by ANY model after 5 stages, and leaderboard() breaks the universal rating tie by dict insertion order (model_tournament.py:232), i.e. first-ever-seen model. cortex/components.py:592-598 then proposes enabling auto_route+model_evolution on this 'confident' evidence.
finding.win_rate_impact: Once the operator accepts the cortex proposal (or flips the flags), LearnedModelRouter overrides the deterministic tier policy with whichever model happened to be recorded first in each bucket — including a model whose builds all ended no_go, since stage success is the only signal and negative build outcomes never demote. Routing then self-reinforces (routed traffic mints more solo wins for the same model), permanently pinning codegen to a possibly-worse model with no path back except manual intervention.
finding.fix: Feed solo appearances from the build's terminal outcome instead of stage success: record play+win only when the final verdict is go, and play+loss (or play-only) on no_go; additionally make RoutingRecommender require at least one contested match (losses+wins from real multi-model comparisons) before recommending.

finding.title: Brief-echo success lessons dominate injection ranking and lock out actionable rules
finding.evidence: Every go build mints '{stack}: successful build — {brief[:120]}' (learning_loop.py:154-157; build dict has no 'notes', so brief is always used — runner.py:4497). Each distinct brief creates a new row (dedupe is exact-text). _inject_lessons pulls top-15 by score DESC (store.py:875-876) then re-ranks by similarity to the CURRENT brief (runner.py:598-607) — and a lesson whose text literally IS an old brief maximally matches any similar new brief in both BM25 and cosine. These content-free rows then get graded helpful on every go (runner.py:6173-6178), permanently boosting their score above newly captured avoid-rules, which start at 0 and can never enter the score-DESC top-15 once ~15 positive-score incumbents exist (no recency or exploration term; un-injected lessons keep times_used=0 so hygiene never retires them either).
finding.win_rate_impact: The 5 lesson slots in every codegen prompt (agents/_common.py:467-475) converge to 'successful build — <old brief>' noise while genuinely actionable gap/avoid lessons are starved forever — the lesson channel consumes prompt budget yet transmits nothing, so recurring defect classes keep failing verification and burning repair retries.
finding.fix: Stop minting the brief-echo lesson (or replace it with a structural note that omits the brief text), and blend recency/exploration into relevant_lessons (e.g. reserve a few of the 15 slots for newest ungraded rows).

finding.title: ExperienceIngestor fills RAG with metadata stubs that recall injects as 'relevant patterns'
finding.evidence: _task_doc (ingestor.py:96-110) ingests "Task 'code' completed by ... task_id=... success=True" for EVERY successful task (~11 per build, no quality filter — _on_task_completed:76-81), and _build_doc (112-132) is only slug/stack/score/verdict/brief metadata. runner._recall (runner.py:866-878) queries top-5 with no score floor, and knowledge_block labels whatever comes back as 'Relevant patterns from the knowledge base (past builds + ingested GitHub repos)' (agents/_common.py:477-489). Because build docs contain 'brief=...' text, they outrank real ingested repo content for any similar new brief.
finding.win_rate_impact: The single RAG channel into codegen prompts carries 'Build X completed, score=88' stubs instead of reusable patterns — top_k=5 slots are crowded out for genuinely useful ingested-repo content, the model is told these stubs are patterns to follow, and manifest.extra['recall_used'] makes this dead channel look like working learning, hiding the loss from the operator.
finding.fix: Drop task-stub ingestion entirely; enrich _build_doc with actual reusable content (entrypoints, file map, distilled practices — the data _distill_win_skill already extracts); tag stub docs with kind metadata and have _recall exclude them or apply a minimum-score floor.

finding.title: Dashboard opens blind mid-build: 50-event WS prime, no REST backfill, no dedup on reconnect
finding.evidence: useEventStream starts with events=[] (api.js:90) and only ever appends live frames without id dedup (api.js:159-164); the server primes just the last 50 events on connect (websockets.py:236). A build emits far more than 50 events (per-stage started/completed, debug attempts, artifact snapshots), so after a mid-build refresh the build.started frame carrying the real stage plan and slug is gone: Studio falls back to the hardcoded stage guess (Studio.jsx:43-52), latestBuildId falls back to any event with a correlation id (buildSignals.js:18-23), and PreviewPanel loses the slug. Every reconnect re-appends the same 50 frames, duplicating rows in Activity and the Overview tail.
finding.win_rate_impact: An operator who opens or refreshes the dashboard during a build sees a wrong pipeline (fabricated stages, no preview, possibly another build's events folded in) and duplicated history after any blip - they misjudge where the build is, cancel healthy builds, or miss real failures scrolled out of the 200-frame buffer.
finding.fix: Dedup by event.id in useEventStream's append, and seed the stream on mount from GET /trajectory?limit=500 (endpoint already exists for Activity replay) before applying live frames.

verdict.evidence: Mechanism real, unfixed in working tree. (1) skyn3t/web/ui/src/api.js:90 starts events=[] and the onmessage append (api.js:159-164) has no id dedup; nothing anywhere seeds the hook from REST — useEventStream is only consumed in App.jsx:95 and shared to all routes. (2) skyn3t/web/websockets.py:236 primes exactly `state.event_bus.history(limit=50)` on every (re)connect in `_serve`; the server-side comment about "no duplicate frames" only covers replay-vs-live within ONE connection. On reconnect the effect closure persists (scheduleReconnect->connect, api.js:181-188), events state is never reset, so the re-primed 50 frames are appended again — duplicate rows in Activity live view (Activity.jsx:119, eventKey uses e.id so dup ids also collide as React keys, Activity.jsx:40-42/298) and Overview's 9-event tail (Overview.jsx:62). (3) A build easily exceeds 50 events: BUILD_STAGE_STARTED/COMPLETED per stage (runner.py:3081,4196,5249; ~8 stages), 3-4 task lifecycle events per stage task (orchestrator.py:141,160; core/agent.py:170,211), STAGE_DEBUG_STARTED/ATTEMPT/RESOLVED and STAGE_ARTIFACT_SNAPSHOT (runner.py:6644,6827,6881), so on a mid-build refresh build.started is routinely outside the 50-frame prime while the bus ring holds 2000 (core/events.py:109-111). One sub-claim is overstated: latestBuildEvents scopes to a single inferred id, so multiple builds are not "folded together" — the risk is picking the wrong latest id, not merging builds. (5) The proposed seed source is valid: GET /api/trajectory exists (routes.py:7509-7535, limit 1..2000), returns Event.to_dict-shaped events with ids always present (routes.py:6440,6514-6520) sorted ascending by (timestamp,id) (routes.py:6521-6528), backed by the 2000-event ring plus durable rows (deps.py:565-589). (a) Dedup in the append: in ws.onmessage replace the setEvents updater with one that drops known ids — `setEvents((prev) => { if (evt && evt.id && prev.some((e) => e.id === evt.id)) return prev; const next = [...prev, evt]; return next.length > maxEvents ? next.slice(next.length - maxEvents) : next; });` (O(maxEvents)=200 per frame; leave setLast untouched — on a reconnect prime the final primed frame is genuinely the latest event). (b) REST seed, merged not replaced: add a separate effect keyed on [maxEvents, authRevision] that best-effort fetches `apiFetch(`/trajectory?limit=${maxEvents}`)` (NOT 500 — the buffer trims to maxEvents=200 anyway) and merges: `setEvents((prev) => { const byId = new Map(); for (const e of [...(data.events||[]), ...prev]) { const k = e && e.id ? e.id : `anon:${e?.timestamp}:${e?.type}`; if (!byId.has(k)) byId.set(k, e); } const merged = [...byId.values()].sort((a,b) => (a?.timestamp||0) - (b?.timestamp||0)); return merged.length > maxEvents ? merged.slice(merged.length - maxEvents) : merged; });` with `.catch(() => {})` and an `alive` cleanup flag — merge (rather than assign) because primed/live WS frames can land before the fetch resolves; /trajectory already returns ascending (timestamp,id) order matching the stream. Do not touch the reconnect/activeSocket/wsRef guard lines — tests pin them verbatim.
